Definition: to root, i.e. strike into the soil, or (by implication) to pluck from it
BiblicalUsage: Taking root is a blessing when God plants, and a curse when the foolish do it. Isaiah says He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root, and Israel shall blossom and bud and fill the face of the world with fruit, and the psalm says God caused His vine to take deep root, and it filled the land. Jeremiah says the wicked have taken root and grow and bring forth fruit, and Job saw the foolish taking root, but suddenly he cursed his habitation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God plants His people to take root, and the root that matters is the one He waters. The foolish can take root for a season, but Job watched it wither, and Jeremiah saw the wicked grow only to be judged. My position is that I want the root God plants, not the root I plant for myself.
